answer: Rewards come from a fixed per-epoch pool split among valid answers: minting identities cannot grow the payout. Each claim must open a memory-hard cipher keyed to its registered key — verified on-ledger — so no solution replays across masks and every head pays a full machine-time bill. Cost is per head, like saffron from hand-picked flowers; still, N machines run N proofs in parallel — honestly linear, not super-linear. Each new mask's slice slides down the ridge to zero while its bill stays flat: farming pays only while a slice tops its price, and only for fixed budgets, not vote weight.
